subject: QuickMart throughput & latency: routing options and pilot next steps
messages:

Subject: QuickMart throughput & latency: routing options and pilot next steps

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the demo call — great context on the recommendation engine use case. Quick recap and a focused set of clarifying questions so we can recommend the best serving route (shared API vs reserved pool):

Key numbers you shared (please correct if I misheard):
- Peak steady QPS: 120 requests/sec (predominantly small prompts ~40 tokens)
- P95 latency target (end-to-end inference): 50–80 ms
- Spiky bursts up to ~240 QPS for ~5–10 minutes 2x/day
- KV cache reuse expected for ~60% of requests (prefix reuse)

Questions that affect the route choice:
1) Is the 50–80 ms target strict for p95 or only for p50 on user-facing flows?
2) Can the product tolerate occasional tail spikes >100 ms during the burst windows if we provide fallback to a slightly faster model?
3) Do you require carrier-grade isolation / dedicated tenancy for compliance or just predictable capacity?

Initial recommendation (high level):
- If p95 <= 80 ms is non-negotiable and spikes are frequent, a Reserved GPU pool (Dedicated) with pinned capacity and local KV cache will be the most consistent fit.
- If you can accept some tail-latency variance and prefer faster time-to-market, start with the Redwood-hosted API (shared) and use intelligent routing + autoscaling; we can route critical flows to a reserved pool later.

Next steps we propose: 1) Quick confirmation of the three clarifying items above. 2) If you confirm p95 constraints, Priyom will draft a short pilot config (reserved vs shared) and a small SLA matrix for your ops team. 3) Book a 30-min follow-up to lock the pilot scope.

I've attached a blank SLA comparison matrix and will follow with a lightweight pilot-config proposal once we hear back.

— Soojin

Subject: Re: QuickMart throughput & latency: routing options and pilot next steps

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the summary and the clear options. Quick answers inline: 

> Is the 50–80 ms target strict for p95 or only for p50 on user-facing flows?
For our core product (search suggestions shown to users) p95 is the target — we try to avoid visible lag. p50 can be lower but we benchmark to p95.

> Can the product tolerate occasional tail spikes >100 ms during the burst windows if we provide fallback to a slightly faster model?
Yes, if the fallback has very similar ranking quality. Ops would prefer fallback rather than a failed response.

> Do you require carrier-grade isolation / dedicated tenancy for compliance or just predictable capacity?
Predictable capacity and data segregation between environments (dev/prod) is the real ask today; full on-prem is not required.

We are open to a short pilot starting with hosted if you can guarantee 99.9% success for p95 < 120 ms during spikes; otherwise we'll consider reserved pool.

I'll ping ops to give access to recent request traces so you can better estimate batch behavior.

— Claire
Claire Huang
Director, Product — QuickMart

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-15T09:20:00Z
Subject: RE: QuickMart throughput & latency: routing options and pilot next steps (technical take)

Fwd: internal technical notes and pilot sketch — attaching config and cost estimate.

(Attachment: pilot-config.yaml, quickmart-pilot-sla-matrix.xlsx, redwood-cost-estimate.pdf)

Hi team —

Thanks Claire for the quick replies. Based on the clarified p95 requirement and tolerance for fallback, here are my thoughts and an explicit pilot plan: 

Technical summary of tradeoffs:
- Shared (Redwood-hosted): Quick to start. We rely on autoscaling + continuous batching. Pros: fast onboarding, cheaper on low steady QPS. Cons: tail latency can vary under burst; caching effectiveness depends on routing locality.
- Reserved pool (Dedicated): Pinned GPUs, local KV cache, lower tail variance. Pros: predictable p95 at the cost of committed spend; easier to control batch window and kernel choices. Cons: higher committed monthly cost.

Quantitative check (back-of-envelope):
- Steady 120 QPS at ~40 tokens => ~4M tokens/min. With continuous batching we can reduce GPU utilization by ~20–30% vs naive.
- Spikes to 240 QPS for 10 minutes: need headroom ~2x for capacity or burst credits. Dedicated sizing option: 2 x A100-equivalent workers (or equivalent multi-GPU nodes) to keep p95 < 80 ms with 60% cache hits. Hosted option: autoscale to similar compute for bursts but p95 risk increases during scale-up window.

Pilot proposal (2 stages):
1) 2-week hosted stress pilot (no long-term commitment): ingest one day's trace replay (ops to provide) and run with our hosted cluster with prefixes cached; success criteria: p95 <= 120 ms for 95% of the trace windows and fallback route latency < 100 ms when used. We will import a sanitized trace to measure real batching behavior.
2) Parallel dedicated baseline test (optional, 3–4 days): allocate one reserved node to run the same trace replay to compare p95 and variance. This gives a clear delta and a data-driven decision.

Deliverables:
- pilot-config.yaml (attached) with model variant, batch window, cache TTL settings
- SLA matrix comparing measurable signals (p50/p95/p99, error rate, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens)
- cost-estimate PDF (committed vs hosted run-rate)

Operational asks for QuickMart:
- Provide a 24-hour hop sample of request traces (anonymized) and a retention window policy for cached prefixes.
- Ops contact for scheduling the replay window (we prefer off-peak dates).

I'll join the follow-up call as the SRE/solutions lead to ensure the pilot config is aligned. Ben / Soojin — I flagged the attachments for the client.

— Priyom

Claire —

Great — thanks for the quick clarity. Per Priyom's plan, here's a proposed timeline and immediate asks: 

1) This week: QuickMart ops uploads a 24-hour anonymized trace to the shared Drive link (I created a folder; link in matrix). Please confirm by end of day which window you can share.
2) Next week (Mon–Fri): Hosted 2-week trace replay pilot begins; we will run continuous replay and report daily p50/p95/p99 and error rates. Priyom will run a parallel 3-day reserved baseline in the middle of the pilot.
3) Success criteria: p95 <= 120 ms for 95% of trace windows AND fallback route < 100 ms when invoked. If met, we'll present a TCO comparison and recommended production path (likely reserved for critical flows + hosted for lower-priority).

Proposed meeting: 30-min pilot kickoff Wednesday 2027-08-18 at 10:00am PT. Does that work?

Thanks — I attached the SLA comparison again for quick review.
